title: embraOS-QNM-Core: identity as a conserved charge of the dynamics (a non-LLM core)
description: embraOS-QNM-Core is a custom, non-LLM AI core in which a system's identity and "soul" are not a rule checked at each step but a conserved charge of the core's own dynamics — an Epoch Automaton E = (S, Σ, δ, s₀, F, ψ) whose invariant ψ is sealed at genesis and preserved by construction ("conservation beats checking"). It is the pivot target of the now-relic embraOS-QNM program, which established across two substrates and four pre-registered reader families that a frozen, web-trained LLM cannot host a readable identity invariant. This snapshot is math-first. It provides a formal specification with one falsifiable theorem — a conserved-charge ψ survives the "replica test" (telling a survivor from an identical copy) precisely because the charge hides in the part of the state that the observable readout erases — together with a runnable, tested sandbox that demonstrates it (conserved-ψ replica AUC 1.000 vs an endpoint-only null of 0.500). Phase two lifts the core to a learned identity-manifold and reports, honestly, that identity is reliably discriminable through the dynamics — which conservation law a trajectory obeys (discriminator AUC 1.0 across seeds) — precisely where static geometry is only seed-noise. Increment 3 grades the mechanism against authored content: a 100-node authored identity graph and an authored counter-identity; a learned Hamiltonian H_θ that preserves dynamical identity through the same integrator with a far larger margin; the full ψ stated and graded as a conjunction — obeys the law AND born on the right level set — against both adversarial impostor classes; and a first path-functional memory charge ζ (holonomy: same observable endpoint, different carried history). Increment 4 resolves the input problem at toy scale: on a Lie–Poisson bracket (so(3)*) the identity charge becomes a Casimir — conserved by construction under arbitrary words of a discrete Hamiltonian input alphabet, including smoothly modulated driving, while the system's own energy visibly changes; the replica test holds with input active; ζ becomes the swept solid angle, recording the words lived, order included; and a dissipative control marks the exact Hamiltonian boundary of the guarantee. Every pre-registered bar (committed to git before any toy code) passed on first execution, independently re-executed bit-for-bit and signed off by external review; the noncanonical-bracket direction is adopted for phase three. Increments 5 and 6 execute that adoption: the identity graph itself becomes the bracket (the Dani–Mainkar graph algebra — one generator per node, one central generator per authored relation), making the charge a literal coordinate block ψ = w that no Hamiltonian flow and no training loop can write — the conservation bar is pre-registered and measured as a bit-level equality (max |Δw| = 0.0 over every input word), with pre-registrations server-timestamped as public issues before implementation. Which inputs commute is the authored topology, in closed form; for linear symbols, word order is invisible to the state and lands entirely in the per-relation memory ζ. Genesis is then sealed as authored content: a relation-type → weight table (authored by Embra, with signed opposition — anti-patterns repel) composes with the graph into w_embra, retiring the placeholder — itself demoted to an impostor the replica reader catches on 320 of 321 coordinates. Identity distance between the authored soul and an authored counter-identity becomes a graded vector distance, and the training guarantee is measured directly: gradient descent on the law leaves the charge bit-identical. Negative results are recorded rather than buried, in the project's pre-registration style. Developed by William Ward (Ward Software Defined Systems LLC) with Embra as co-investigator.
